packaging: isolate x86 LLVM flags and support release archives

QB 1214821 failed in Source1005 when Base-Dev GCC project flags
reached the forced Clang build. Its release mode also removes DWARF
options that the archive converter previously required.

Pin the x86_64 compile and link policy to the effective Toolchain
command from QB 1215143. Preserve project architecture options and
the existing debug/release choice. Match whole tokens: report the
established cleanup in TIZEN_LLVM_NORMALIZED_FLAGS and extra rejected
project options in TIZEN_LLVM_DROPPED_FLAGS. Do not alter other arches.

Accept an original command without any debug option as release and
omit debug emission flags from archive conversion. Keep DWARF-4
certification when debug options exist and reject unknown options.
Reject unexpected debug sections in a converted release object.

Qualification must compare exact Toolchain flag strings, compiler
identities, all RPM payloads and 90 translation units against the
certified build. The local configure string lacks the explicit
function/data-section flags present in the QB input; do not infer
binary identity from configuration alone.

packaging: optimize x86_64 clang with BOLT

Enable BOLT by default on x86_64: ordinary install, snapshot, append
bolt configuration, certify the dry-run and parallel llvm-bolt build,
relink with emit-relocs, strip debug, rewrite, tiny/real checks, strip
all, RUNPATH repair, debug-mode debuglink, security and tiny/real
checks, compare-root, native archive conversion, candidate replacement,
one unchanged platform post chain, and the post gate. Only after
compare-root may BOLT change the buildroot. Other architectures retain
the baseline behavior. Roll back in Quickbuild with the one-line
bcond_without -> bcond_with change; Source1200/1201 are declared
unconditionally because gbs inserts generated Patch declarations after
the last Source line, and conditional Sources would hide those
declarations on other architectures and when BOLT is disabled.
BOLT-specific BuildRequires remain guarded by the same x86_64 BOLT
condition, leaving binary packages on other architectures unchanged
while adding these two files to the source package. --without clang_bolt
is available for local builds. Only enabled %build adds -d keeprsp. No
project configuration change is required.

No disk-space thresholds are imposed; each stage records free space. A
candidate preparation failure prevents its installation. Installation or
post-processing failures abort the RPM build; the failed BUILDROOT is
not rolled back as a whole. Diagnostics report available evidence and
requirements/shortfall estimated from actual file sizes measured in this
build. A readable log without disk-failure evidence is unconfirmed; an
unavailable log is unknown. Release the in-tree ThinLTO cache after the
compare-root gate passes.

The binary Source is the existing profile v2, trained on 13 ARM plus 10
AArch64 source files. Compressed size 9,735,212 bytes; SHA256
52fd8522b8cceadebfb6bfc0a19f721f1072cff95c682b12b2c4dd5b0cc1e27f.
Uncompressed SHA256:
d9b132f9430dfed32e080c65b4422bd76eba4a9c2101a2b18a7f66c94133b326.
Certify 111 BOLT task descriptions plus two TF refresh tasks: CMake
rewrites the TF anchor, while its archive is restored from the prebuilt
artifact and must retain its SHA. Unknown work fails closed.
R=(S+U)/(N+U) and S/N must each be <=5%, without infer-stale; profile
coverage N/M is about 16%.

Preserve ELF type/interpreter, RELRO coverage and flags, GNU_STACK
flags, GNU_PROPERTY/note contents, dynamic flags/BIND_NOW,
RPATH/RUNPATH, NEEDED, W+X status, dynsym interfaces and symbol
versions. Both qualification ELFs lack .note.gnu.property: this build
did not enable CET independently of BOLT. The local qualification
candidate uses the historical same-source llvm-bolt; delivery builds its
own llvm-bolt in the tree.

Historical LLVM C++ -O3 single-file qualification used 30 rows from 20
distinct sources, five samples per side, alternating roles at the same
compiler path/inode. Candidate/ordinary geometric mean: x86_64
0.855890085, ARM 0.856351167, AArch64 0.847699213. x86_64
independent-20/holdout-10: 0.854398975/0.858880117. ARM
independent-20/holdout-10: 0.858165628/0.868458776; AArch64
independent-20/holdout-10: 0.847858623/0.847902567. These are historical
measurements, not a remeasurement of the final debuglink artifact; they
cover this LLVM workload, not general application or runtime
performance. With -use-old-text the packaged clang is 152,532,400 bytes,
12,602,968 bytes (+9.0%) larger than the stripped ordinary clang; the
.gnu_debuglink section adds 104 bytes.

The final clang has no .symtab, DWARF sections or BOLT identity note. In
debug builds, clang-debuginfo supplies matching function symbols in
clang-22.debug, linked from the executable by a verified .gnu_debuglink
and CRC. Use eu-strip because LLVM only-keep-debug crashes with SIGSEGV
(-11) on the BOLT ELF segment layout. The symbol file provides
function-level localization, not source lines. Verify the full symtab
and cold-fragment addresses, unchanged program headers and loaded
sections, and both installed SHAs. Release builds retain fully stripped
clang without a symbol file or debuglink. Debugsource still omits these
five clang-exclusive sources (ordinary DWARF proof retained):
build/tools/clang/tools/driver/clang-driver.cpp,
clang/tools/driver/cc1_main.cpp, clang/tools/driver/cc1as_main.cpp,
clang/tools/driver/cc1gen_reproducer_main.cpp,
clang/tools/driver/driver.cpp. In release builds, where no symbol file
is shipped, crash localization requires the build-side identity/rewrite
records, the pre-strip BOLT ELF, the matching ordinary ELF, and the tool
and profile identities.

An earlier revision completed %install on Quickbuild x86_64; this
revision is pending Quickbuild verification. Still open: full
release-mode build; accel/worker identity; cleanup cannot be guaranteed
without matching /proc; performance outside LLVM workloads. The Ninja
job limit does not cap linker memory. Maintenance notes: header of
packaging/clang-bolt-helper.py

Match the BOLT candidate RUNPATH to the ordinary CMake-installed clang
using an in-place CMake RPATH_CHANGE and preserve all other ELF bytes.
Build llvm-bolt in parallel with the existing build job limit and verify
the exact task set independently of completion order. Check real LLVM C
and C++ objects before strip, before install and after RPM processing.

Adopt -use-old-text: compared with the previous appended-text layout
(183,224,160 bytes), clang is 16.75% smaller at 152,532,296 bytes before
the debuglink, with identical generated object files.

Handle SIGTERM and SIGHUP cooperatively and clean up the command process
group before exiting. Freeze all ELF bytes outside the original
RUNPATH/RPATH string ranges during path repair. Compare all ELF/program
header fields and LOAD bytes across strip-all, normalizing only e_shoff,
e_shnum and e_shstrndx because strip relocates the nonloaded section
table. Require the platform debugfiles.list to contain clang-22.debug in
debug-mode post checks. Bound each run-step command to 14400 seconds,
reporting its step name and elapsed time on timeout. Preserve unexpected
helper exceptions with a diagnostic and traceback.

cmake: use hybrid LLVM linkage on x86_64

Enable shared LLVM and Clang linkage in the x86_64 recipe while keeping
clang, lld and llvm-ar statically linked to LLVM components. Their
driver aliases continue to share the same executable. Other tools use
libLLVM and, where applicable, libclang-cpp through the normal upstream
interfaces.

Use TIZEN_HYBRID_LINK and a per-consumer TIZEN_STATIC_LLVM property to
select component dependencies only for the three opted-in drivers. When
disabled, the shared-link interfaces retain upstream behavior. Keep
BUILD_SHARED_LIBS and the unified LLVM driver disabled on x86_64.

Preserve upstream forced-static llvm-tblgen, clang-tblgen, lldb-tblgen,
llvm-config and llvm-exegesis. Tool-private archives and build utilities
retain upstream behavior. Do not change armv7l or aarch64 recipes,
optimization flags, the static-devel %files rules or native archive conversion.

Validation of the original hybrid implementation: local full GBS build
produced 22 binary RPMs and one source RPM. The 188-entry NEEDED table
had 183 passes, four non-default targets not produced, and one accepted
--as-needed exception (AnnotateFunctions.so). Native archives passed
225/225 checks and 90 complete objects were byte-identical. See docs/53
in the validation evidence. Quickbuild verification remains pending.

Add a post-build NEEDED assertion for the three component-linked drivers.
A complete-recipe configuration probe found no empty component lists
among 96 rewritten static interfaces; fail configuration if one appears.
